links.note: The chapter's opening Kautilya quotation is about a kingdom's material base - fertile land, mines, forests, water. 30654 is the concept for that base (surplus food is what lets people do anything other than farm); the set has no Kautilya or statecraft concept of its own.

How rulers were chosen: hereditary in monarchies, selected by the assembly in ganas - 30657 is the concept that a raja could be chosen rather than born to it. 30656 is the assembly's decision-making, one step earlier.
Janapadas merging into mahajanapadas by the 7th-6th century BCE - 30652.
What 'gana' or 'sangha' implies: 30658 is the concept that gives these states their name and marks that monarchy was not the only form.
The four varnas and what is not one of them - 30664.
The exception is that a monarchical raja was not elected by citizens, so the item turns on 30657's distinction between inherited and selected rulership.
Matching mahajanapadas to their regions draws on 30652's list of sixteen stretching from Gandhara eastward. 30653 is the further step of reading a reason off their concentration.
The false pairing defines jati by religious belief; the item rests on 30664's birth-and-occupation ordering of varna and jati.
A trader running from the northwest through the Ganga plains to the east is on the Uttarapatha, named in 30668.
Fortifications and moats read as a sign of conflict is exactly 30660, where the evidence for warfare between mahajanapadas is weighed.
Definition of sabha/samiti as the deciding assembly - 30656; 30657 is the narrower point that such an assembly also picked the raja.
Naming the Uttarapatha - 30668.
A state whose ruler is chosen by a voting assembly is classified as a gana or sangha - 30658.
Walls and moats as emphasis on defence - the warfare evidence of 30660.
Keyed on jati as an occupational group - 30664.
The barrier on the way south is the Vindhyas, which 30668 names on the Dakshinapatha.
The false pairing calls Vajji a hereditary monarchy; the item rests on Vajji being a gana, which is 30658.
Rajagriha as Magadha's capital - part of the mahajanapada inventory in 30652.
People, ideas and teachings moving with goods is 30668's point that these routes carried trade, pilgrimage and armies alike.
Cultivable land, mines, timber, pastures and water attributed to Kautilya - the same epigraph as the other Kautilya items, housed on the resource-base concept 30654.
Rajagriha, Kaushambi, Takshashila and Shishupalgarh are Second Urbanisation cities; the false option calls Shishupalgarh Harappan, which is precisely the distinction 30648 draws.

The visible statement, that changing occupation was impossible, is the false one - it turns on 30664's account of varna-jati as a historical development rather than a fixed order. DEFECT: statements 1 and 3 are missing from the stored stem.
'Metallurgy' is glossed in this chapter where iron replaces bronze - 30659.
Guilds of traders and craftspeople are society organising itself by occupation, which is 30662's list (trade, farming, crafts). 30651 is trade as the driver of janapada growth, not its organisation.
Keyed on raja as 'hereditary or selected' ruler, which is 30657's distinction.
Ujjayini as Avanti's capital - the mahajanapada inventory, 30652.
The merged larger states are the mahajanapadas - 30652.
The water-filled moat is part of the defensive evidence in 30660.
Naming Vajji or Malla as a gana/sangha - 30658.
The raja selected by the assembly - 30657 states exactly this.
Jati as an inherited occupational community - 30664.
Uttarapatha named - 30668.
Dakshinapatha named - 30668.
Shishupalgarh as the Kalinga capital, one of the cities of the Second Urbanisation - 30648.
How janapadas formed - clans sharing language and custom settling a territory under a raja, which is 30649.
Ramparts, moat and narrow gateways described - the defensive evidence of 30660.
Roles of the four varnas - 30664.
Shishupalgarh's square plan and planned streets: a city of the Second Urbanisation, 30648. 30646 is the Harappan order that had been lost.
The political landscape by 300 BCE - the mahajanapada phase ending, which is the arc 30652 sets up.
Analysis of the Kautilya epigraph's security, economy and resource requirements - the material-base concept 30654, as with the other Kautilya items in this file.
Magadha against Vajji is monarchy against gana - 30658, which exists precisely to record that monarchy was not the only form.
What the Arthashastra epigraph shows about the era's statecraft concerns - resources, water, food security; 30654.

A ruler balancing Vedic ritual against donations to Buddhist monasteries popular with merchants and artisans: the item is read through how the society was organised into groups by religion and occupation, 30662.
